newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Waikato bus home the Log, look to defence.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Waikato bus home the Log, look to defence.

text.p: HAMILTON, Sept 9 - The Waikato rugby team bussed home to Hamilton with the Ranfurly Shield today after celebrating long and hard last night with the Taranaki team they took it from, NZPA reports.
In stark contrast to their five previous Shield wins, including four against Auckland at Eden Park, there was a feeling of mutual admiration among the players from both teams.
Up to 5000 Waikato supporters journeyed to New Plymouth's Rugby Park -- the "Bull Ring" -- to cheer their team on to a 40-19, four-tries-to-two victory as part of a raucous, colourful 28,000 crowd.

They, like the team, partied afterwards, but the Waikato team did their celebrating with their opposition once the formalities were over, the Shield locked firmly under the burly arm of its official keeper for now, reserve prop Craig Stevenson.

"The two teams were together last night along with a lot of supporters and even the Taranaki players felt Waikato had deserved to win -- that they had something a little bit more than they had," Waikato team manager Steve Gilbert said today.
"But Taranaki played with such passion that it's fair to say our players hold them in a lot of respect," he said.
Taranaki Rugby Union expect to net nearly $500,000 from their two Ranfurly Shield defences and they and their supporters were philosophical about losing the coveted Log o' Wood so soon.

While face-painted, colour-waving supporters scrambled for a view of the spectacle in the natural amphitheatre of the "Bull Ring", hundreds of banners proclaiming Ferdinand's superiority to Mooloo were paraded around the stadium and the mascot himself arrived by amber and black helicopter, blowing similar coloured smoke, as an electric pre-match atmosphere built.
There was certainly no willingness on the part of the Taranaki team to give the Shield up without a fight.

"I don't think I've ever been hit that hard by a team in the first five or 10 minutes -- they just came out like men possessed. I'm just proud of my guys for the way they defended," Waikato captain Steve Gordon said.
Meanwhile, Waikato's first defence of the Ranfurly Shield this Friday night has quickly been dubbed the "Battle of the Chiefs" and there may be more to it than just traditional rivalry.
Waikato will defend the Ranfurly Shield against an All Black-studded North Harbour side under temporary floodlights at Hamilton's Rugby Park on Black Friday -- September 13.

The New Zealand Rugby Union board of directors will make a choice between the homes of Waikato and North Harbour on Wednesday when it decides where to base the Chiefs Super 12 team next year. The Chiefs' present home is Hamilton.
"I certainly hope that doesn't overshadow the game. It's not a situation I'm sure either North Harbour or Waikato really wish to be in," Waikato coach John Boe said.

Having taken the Shield from Taranaki for the first time -- its previous wins have been over Auckland (4) and North Auckland -- Waikato is set to play the first Friday Shield match and the first under lights.
